passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Guinea.

source.name: Police de l'Air et des Frontières

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of all arriving travellers and is checked at Conakry airport and land borders.

source.name: Police de l'Air et des Frontières

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not checked at the border, but comprehensive medical cover including evacuation is strongly advised — hospital care in Guinea is very limited.

source.name: Police de l'Air et des Frontières

onwardTicket.text: Not systematically checked, but the e-visa application asks for travel details and border officers may ask to see a return or onward ticket.

source.name: Police de l'Air et des Frontières

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; officers may ask visitors to show sufficient means for their stay.

source.name: Police de l'Air et des Frontières

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency should be declared on arrival, and exporting Guinean francs is restricted — confirm the current limits with your airline or a Guinean embassy before travel.

source.name: Police de l'Air et des Frontières

payments.text: Guinea runs on cash — cards are accepted only at a handful of Conakry hotels and ATMs are unreliable. Bring euros or US dollars to exchange, and expect to carry large bundles of francs.

safety.text: Guinea has been governed by a military transition since the 2021 coup. Demonstrations in Conakry can turn violent and internet access is periodically restricted — avoid protests, keep documents on you and monitor your embassy's advice.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Guinea Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to April is the dry season and the practical window for travel — the Fouta Djallon highlands are at their best; the June–October rains make many roads impassable.

tips.text: Apply for the e-visa only on the official border-police portal paf.gov.gn — third-party visa websites charge heavy markups and some are outright scams.
Avoid demonstrations and large gatherings, especially in Conakry — protests linked to the post-2021 political transition can turn violent at short notice.
Your yellow fever certificate is checked on arrival — travellers without one can be vaccinated on the spot at a fee or turned back.
Plan your money before arrival: bring clean euro or dollar notes, change what you need in Conakry, and do not count on ATMs working outside the capital.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Guinea?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do. Guinea issues visas almost entirely online — apply for an e-visa on the official portal paf.gov.gn before travel. Citizens of the 15 ECOWAS countries are exempt and enter freely under the bloc's free-movement protocol.

faq.question: How does the Guinea e-visa work?
faq.answer: You apply on paf.gov.gn, the portal of Guinea's border police, upload your passport details and pay online — a single-entry tourist e-visa is commonly reported at around USD 80. Approval usually takes a few working days and the visa is finalised with biometrics on arrival.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Guinea?
faq.answer: No — visas are no longer routinely issued on arrival. Apply for the e-visa online before travelling; airlines will normally refuse boarding without an approved e-visa or an ECOWAS passport.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Guinea?
faq.answer: Yes. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of all arriving travellers regardless of nationality, and it is checked at Conakry airport.

faq.question: Is Guinea safe to visit?
faq.answer: Guinea is calm across most of the country but politically volatile — a military government has been in power since 2021, and demonstrations in Conakry can turn violent. Most visits are trouble-free with sensible precautions; check your government's travel advice before booking.
